subject: Prefetch fallback causing latency spikes — playbook & rollout ask

Subject: Re: quick heads-up — spike in latency tied to prefetch fallback

Jonas —

Quick note from our SREs this morning: since the update you rolled last week we saw a repeatable latency spike on our inference route when the client-side prefix hits prefetch fallback (requests that trigger an early KV cache miss and cause the runtime to switch to non-prefetch path). TPMs recorded 200-300ms extra p50 on conversational flows; p95 is worse. We've attached a small repro trace.

This is blocking our peak-hour SLA for a portion of traffic. Can your team advise whether there is a safe rollback or an on-the-fly mitigation? We're trying to avoid a full revert if we can.

Thanks —
Sam
Samantha Li
Head of ML Ops, ClearPath AI

Key asks for platform/runtime:

- Is there a short-term runtime config toggle (per-tenant) to disable prefetch without redeploying model weights? (Logan)

I attached the trace they sent. I'm happy to join a quick call with Sam + SREs.

Action: Karthik, can you triage and propose immediate mitigations today? If we need a temporary exception (disable prefetch for CP) we should get a clear playbook and comms.

— Jonas

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: quick heads-up — spike in latency tied to prefetch fallback

Thanks for the ping — dug into the trace and reproduced locally on a dev rig. Quick summary of findings: 

- Root cause (probable): prefetch->fallback path introduces a synchronous KV materialization step when the prefix length crosses an internal boundary; under certain cache miss patterns that forces an extra serialize/deserialize and a short mutex wait. That maps to the 150-300ms delta Sam observed.
- Short-term mitigation (fast): we can add a per-tenant runtime flag to force "prefer_non_prefetch" for affected workloads. This is a config toggle we can ship without touching model artifacts; it routes requests to the non-prefetch code path at request admission. Estimated dev + safe rollout: ~6 hours including a limited canary.
- Alternate mitigation (safer for wide rollout): tune the async buffer window to reduce the probability of entering the expensive materialization state. That is lower-risk but requires a runtime patch and broader validation (estimated 2-3 days).

I attached a short repro and a diagnostic script. Proposed immediate plan:
1) Ship per-tenant flag for ClearPath: prefer_non_prefetch=true on CP-2026-119. Canary on 1% of traffic for 30m, then 10%/1h, then 100% if stable.
2) Notify product/console team to expose the toggle in the tenant UI and add audit log entries. (Marissa, can you coordinate the customer comms?)
3) Begin longer-term buffer tuning after we stabilize the toggle.

Risks: the non-prefetch path has slightly higher avg token cost (~3-5%) for affected flows; we should capture cost delta in the canary.

I'll prep a short runbook for the on-call to execute the toggle and rollback steps. If you want, I can also join a customer call in 30m.

— Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime

Attachments: clearpath_prefetch_incident_notes.pdf, repro_small_trace.txt, canary_toggle_script.sh (referenced)
